source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA9 publishes 38 MW of IT capacity across 700,000 square feet of technical space in Sterling, Virginia. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 38 MW supports roughly 950 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation baseline, the same load supports roughly 3,800 racks. The arithmetic is straightforward but the right answer depends entirely on how the space is configured, and the operator publishes no density figure. No certifications are listed on the spec page.

NVA9 ranks third by published IT capacity among the five facilities in Virginia for which this site has read a megawatt figure, out of 326 Virginia facilities mapped in total. Those five facilities together publish 233 MW, and NVA9's 38 MW represents roughly 16 percent of that published total. Because most mapped facilities publish no figure, both the rank and the share describe only the visible slice of the state's capacity, not the full picture.

Sterling sits inside the Northern Virginia corridor, which is the largest data center market in the United States by most industry measures, though this site holds no independent megawatt total for the corridor to confirm that claim from its own data. What the numbers do show is that 700,000 square feet of technical space is a large footprint for a single campus code, and 38 MW against that area implies relatively low average density, leaving physical room that could support denser AI workloads if power is available. Whether additional power has been contracted or is accessible at this site is not published.
